name: Space Skipping and Empty Volume Culling
text:
# Space Skipping and Empty Volume Culling

Also called: Empty Space Skipping, Volume Culling

## Overview
Space Skipping and Empty Volume Culling refers to a family of [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) techniques in volume rendering that reduce computational load by identifying and excluding primitives, voxels, or ray segments that do not contribute to the final image. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Hierarchical Bounding Box Tree for Empty-Space Skipping](8182-hierarchical-bounding-box-tree-for-empty-space-skipping.md) by encompassing a broader range of strategies, including geometric bounding volumes, visibility masks, and parallel segment lists, rather than relying solely on hierarchical tree traversal. It differs from [Early Termination and Probabilistic Path Control](1791-early-termination-and-probabilistic-path-control.md) by focusing on pre-computed or geometrically derived exclusion zones rather than just dynamic ray state termination.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism shared by all children is the reduction of work units (samples, voxels, or pixels) processed per frame while maintaining acceptable visual fidelity [G]. This is achieved through three primary strategies:
1. **Culling/Skipping:** Identifying regions of the volume or ray path that do not contribute to the final image (e.g., empty space, occluded voxels) and bypassing their evaluation.
2. **Termination:** Halting the integration loop when the accumulated contribution becomes negligible (e.g., high opacity, low transmittance) [S1, unofficial].
3. **Adaptation:** Varying the computational effort based on local scene complexity or global performance budgets [S1, unofficial].

Mathematically, these methods modify the [standard front-to-back compositing](#1141-front-to-back-compositing-unpremultiplied.md) loop:
$$ C_{acc} = C_{acc} + C_{sample} \cdot \alpha_{sample} \cdot (1 - \alpha_{acc}) $$
$$ \alpha_{acc} = \alpha_{acc} + \alpha_{sample} \cdot (1 - \alpha_{acc}) $$
by introducing conditions that break the loop early, skip iterations, or reduce the number of $C_{sample}$ queries.

## Subtopics

### [Parallel Ray Casting with Segment Lists](2565-parallel-ray-casting-with-segment-lists.md)
[Parallel Ray Casting with Segment Lists](#2565-parallel-ray-casting-with-segment-lists.md) is a distributed-memory and shared-memory parallel volume rendering algorithm that accelerates ray casting by precomputing lists of occupied volume segments to skip empty space. It distributes image rows across MPI ranks and OpenMP threads, calculating sampling points based on a derived step length. It differs from siblings like [SparseLeap](5152-sparseleap.md) by using explicit segment lists derived from volume geometry rather than sparse voxel [octree traversal](#1587-octree-traversal.md) or occupancy misses, and from [Visibility Culling](6226-visibility-culling.md) by operating at the ray-segment level rather than tile or view-frustum level. See [Parallel Ray Casting with Segment Lists](2565-parallel-ray-casting-with-segment-lists.md).

### [Visibility Culling](6226-visibility-culling.md)
[Visibility Culling](#6226-visibility-culling.md) is a family of acceleration techniques in volume rendering that reduces computational load by identifying and excluding primitives, voxels, or ray segments that do not contribute to the final image. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Bounding Volume Empty-Space Culling](17140-bounding-volume-empty-space-culling.md) by focusing on optical or geometric visibility relative to the camera, rather than purely on geometric emptiness, and from [Early Termination and Probabilistic Path Control](1791-early-termination-and-probabilistic-path-control.md) by often operating on pre-computed or screen-space visibility masks rather than just dynamic ray state. See [Visibility Culling](6226-visibility-culling.md).

### [Bounding Volume Empty-Space Culling](17140-bounding-volume-empty-space-culling.md)
[Bounding Volume Empty-Space Culling](#17140-bounding-volume-empty-space-culling.md) restricts volume reconstruction computation to the "effective" reconstruction area by calculating an initial bounding volume and slicing it according to the viewing direction, using these slices as a depth buffer to guide reconstruction. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Hierarchical Bounding Box Tree for Empty-Space Skipping](8182-hierarchical-bounding-box-tree-for-empty-space-skipping.md) by using a simple geometric approximation (truncated shapes) rather than a hierarchical [tree structure](#4139-tree-based-structures-octree-pointer-tree-sparse-voxel-dag.md), and from [Occupancy Mask Culling](#occupancy-mask-culling) by being an approximation rather than an exact mask of projection data shadows. See [Bounding Volume Empty-Space Culling](17140-bounding-volume-empty-space-culling.md).

### Parsimonious Ray Sampling and Fused Rendering
**Definition:** A rendering optimization that infers [ray-BBox intersection](#772-ray-box-intersection.md) to sample query points only within the scene bounding box, applicable only to bounded scenes [S1, unofficial].
**Steps:** Fuse approximately ten point-wise operations for the forward and backward pass of the [density-to-alpha](#3052-raw2alpha-density-to-alpha-conversion.md) function conversion [S1, unofficial]. In the volume rendering accumulation, halt tracking a ray once the accumulated transmittance falls below $10^{-3}$ [S1, unofficial].

### Surface Localization Acceleration
**Definition:** Acceleration methods that localize the surface interface and concentrate samples only in relevant regions, effectively skipping empty space, because only 10-20% of evaluated samples have non-zero density [S2].
**Steps:** Refine the sampling strategy to focus solely on the localized surface [S2].
**Comparison:** [Standard volumetric rendering](#1362-nerf-rendering-formula.md) is inefficient because it samples the entire ray; surface localization reduces the number of required MLP evaluations by skipping empty space [S2].

### Per-ray Volume Culling
**Definition:** Optimization to avoid visiting every volume at every step. Previously, the march visited every volume at every step just to ask cell_index whether it was inside, and almost always was not. The new method builds an active list up front, so a step only visits volumes whose t-range contains it [S3, unofficial].
**Comparison:** Differs from the previous approach which visited every volume at every step. The new approach is pure work elimination and produces byte-identical output [S3, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of skipping empty space in volume rendering dates back to the early days of ray casting, where the primary goal was to avoid sampling voxels with zero density. Early methods relied on simple bounding boxes or grid-based occupancy flags. As rendering hardware evolved, more sophisticated structures like hierarchical bounding box trees and sparse voxel octrees were introduced to handle larger and more complex datasets [S1, unofficial]. The rise of [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) and implicit representations has renewed interest in these techniques, leading to methods like parsimonious ray sampling and surface localization acceleration that integrate culling directly into the learning and rendering pipeline [S1, unofficial][S2]. Parallel implementations have further optimized these techniques for distributed and multi-threaded environments, enabling real-time rendering of large-scale volumetric data [S1, unofficial].

## Sources

[S2] Recent Advances and Trends in Learning‐Based 3D Representations, https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.70530, fetched 2026-10-26
[S3] cvcGL VolRenNode, CUDA raycast backend, and the volren_bunny demo, https://github.com/transfix/libcvc/pull/323, fetched 2026-10-25 (unofficial)
